newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin tells rival Caucasus leaders to make peace.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin tells rival Caucasus leaders to make peace.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin ordered the squabbling leaders of two regions in Russia's volatile North Caucasus on Friday to make peace or lose his support in coming elections.

Russian news agencies quoted Yeltsin as telling the leaders of North Ossetia and Ingushetia to sign an agreement ruling out any territorial claims on each other for 15 to 20 years. Tensions between the two regions have risen in recent weeks.

"I want you to end this undeclared war between you today, once and for all," RIA news agency quoted Yeltsin as telling Ingush President Ruslan Aushev and North Ossetia leader Akhsarbek Galazov at a meeting in the Kremlin.

"Either you will have our support and the personal support of the Russian president in the election campaign period or you will not get it. I think this is quite serious, so you should drop your personal differences and sign the prepared agreement."
Both leaders face re-election next year.
Nearly 200 people were killed in 1992 in fighting over the Prigorodny district in North Ossetia. The district, which lies close to the regional capital of Vladikavkaz, used to belong to Ingushetia.

The Ingushis were deported from their land in 1944 by Soviet dictator Josef Stalin and returned in the 1950s to find that some of their land, including Prigorodny, was under the jurisdiction of North Ossetia.
The latest clashes involved Ingushis trying to resettle in the district.
They have revived fears that the conflict will flare up again and prompted the Kremlin last month to issue calls for compromise and calm.
Ingushetia and North Ossetia both border Chechnya, where Russian troops fought separatists for nearly 21 months until August last year.

Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying the problems in Prigorodny should be settled immediately. He said he had no intention of increasing the number of Russian interior or defence ministry troops in North Ossetia or Ingushetia.
